chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Fuḍayl narrated from Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the muhrim and what he may kill among the creatures.

He said: "He may kill the black snake, the viper, the mouse, the scorpion, and every snake. If a predatory beast attacks you, then kill it; and if it does not attack you, then do not kill it. And the vicious dog—if it attacks you, then kill it. There is no harm for the muhrim to throw at the kite, and if robbers confront him, he may defend himself against them."

key_terms.ٱلْأَفْعَى: a viper; a dangerous venomous snake
key_terms.ٱلْمُحْرِمِ: a person in the state of ihram during hajj or 'umrah

ai.seo_question: What animals may a muhrim kill while in the state of ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings for a person in ihram regarding harmful animals and self-defense. It permits killing certain dangerous creatures, allows defending oneself against attacking beasts and robbers, and forbids killing predatory animals when they pose no threat.
